To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the water-sorption characteristics of disintegrants are important determinants of the dissolution properties of direct compression tablets, and the dissolution properties of tablets can be predicted from the water-sorbability of the disintegrant used.
the water-sorption and dissolution properties of tablet disintegrate powders are not predictive of the disintegration and dissolution properties of compressed tablets containing the disintegrants.
the water-sorption characteristics of tablet disintegrators are important in the design of direct compression formulations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the water-sorption and dissolution properties of disintegrants in tablet formulations.
the effect of disintegrants upon the dissolution of calcium phosphate dibasic tablets, and the effect of water vapor upon the physical properties of the tablets.
the effect of tablet disintegrating agents on the dissolution of calcium phosphate dibasic tablets, and the effect of water vapor on the disintegrating agents in tablets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of sodium starch glycolates and cation-exchange resins with calcium phosphate dibasic tablets will result in a more rapid disintegration than starch or carboxymethyl cellulose.
the water-sorption and disintegration properties of disintegrants are not necessarily related to the disintegrant's ability to effect dissolution of the drug from a compressed tablet.
sodium starch glycolates and cation-exchange resins are superior to starch and carboxymethyl cellulose as tablet disintegrants in formulations containing calcium phosphate dibasic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the water-sorption behavior of disintegrants is a key factor in their effectiveness and should be considered in the design of tablets containing these materials.

sodium starch glycolates, cation-exchange resins, or other materials that absorb water from the surrounding environment, should not be used in the formulation of tablets prepared from water-soluble matrixes.
the disintegrant should be selected on the basis of its effect upon the dissolution of the tablet formulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the water-sorption and tablet-disintegration properties of disintegrants are closely related.
the water-sorption behavior of a disintegrant can be used to predict the dissolution and disintegration behavior of tablets prepared using a direct compression matrix.
the water-sorption characteristics of the tablet disintegrant should be considered during the formulation process.
